description: The registered process returns an accepted job receipt in data.job_id and data.status=queued. Retain that exact canonical id and read service_interface::job_service::get_job until terminal. The stored job.result is the original operation envelope, including data and structured error; job.error is also retained on failure. A receipt does not establish a session, dispatch row, or successful first turn. launch_busy names the current operation/job and starts no work. Fleet session-management Phase B, D1+D2 (§4). Validates role_class (ephemeral | project | principal — primary/chat are never spawn-assigned), work_class, and budget_line; when role_name is given, checks the fill-never-mint rule for principal offices (role_not_legislated when no role row exists yet) and the reserved <solet>-Main mint guard (reserved_role_name). Writes the managed_session ledger row in 'spawning' state BEFORE resolving and dispatching through the host driver, so a half-failed spawn stays visible rather than silently disappearing. Three host drivers ship: 'operator' (degenerate, observes via registration only, never spawns), 'headless' (D1 — spawns an actual Claude Code process over stream-json, config-gated fail-closed on a resolved permission mode/.mcp.json/the claude binary), and 'tmux' (D2 — spawns a detached tmux session running the interactive claude CLI, config-gated fail-closed on the tmux binary/version plus the same claude-launch checks as headless; its spawn() also runs a bounded PTY-confirm expect loop for the interactive --dangerously-load-development-channels prompt, fail-closed on timeout). Host choice affects deploy survival: a 'headless' worker is swap-mortal by construction (a direct child of the platform process, killed unconditionally on every platform stop including a blue-green deploy's quiesce step) while a 'tmux' worker is swap-durable by construction (its pane belongs to the independent tmux daemon, untouched by the platform's stop/swap path) — prefer 'tmux' for any worker expected to outlive a single release; a deploy holding live headless workers needs an explicit quiesce-or-accept decision recorded in the deploy reason. Optional provider_env (an object of environment names to string values) selects the Claude provider backend for this one worker. It is accepted only for runtime claude_code on the tmux host, where it is applied to the pane's own environment on new-session -e; it is refused with provider_selection_not_applied_by_host on the headless and operator hosts, and with provider_unsupported_for_runtime for any other runtime. An overlay key that names a managed worker variable is refused, naming the key only. The values are never written to the persisted job payload, the ledger row, the spawn detail or any log line. Known limit: the values are visible to local process listings (ps) for the instant of the tmux new-session call, as the identity variables already are. Refusals surface as a failed launch job, not at admission, because the overlay is taken out before preflight. A spawn-time PreToolUse tool allowlist mechanism exists (allowed_tools, or resolved per_work_class from plugin.yaml's work_class_tool_allowlists) — an out-of-allowlist tool call is denied with a clean error, never executed and never a silent hang — but per operator ruling (2026-08-03, 'we don't have any restrictions now') it ships UNARMED by default: an empty/unconfigured allowlist means no extra restriction, not a lockdown. The permission mode itself (plugin.yaml's headless_permission_mode) similarly accepts any value today; the driver only refuses when no mode resolves at all. The tmux driver denies Claude Code's structured-choice AskUserQuestion tool by default (operator ruling, 2026-08-14 — its blocking picker stalls an unattended or peer-driven session); allow_askuserquestion=true lifts the deny for that one spawn. The headless driver needs no equivalent: measured live, its stream-json mode never enumerates the tool in the first place, so the flag is inert there. The codex runtime has no equivalent tool at all. W6 (#13 §44.3, 2026-08-14): local_name is the name the spawned worker answers to on its OWN machine — the headless driver's --name and the tmux driver's --name plus the label its session name derives from. Omitted, it defaults to role_name for a project-class role and to lane_id otherwise. Git-Controller is a project-class role, not a principal one: a `plugin::agent_messaging_plugin::provision_role_session` call with role_name='Git-Controller' and no requested_role_class resolves it to project and assigns local_name='Git-Controller'. This is what lets a spawned Git-Controller pass the git mutation guard IMMEDIATELY, on its first turn, instead of needing a second driven turn to claim its name first: the guard resolves its caller by reading the local session file's 'name' field and comparing it EXACTLY, so the worker has to be born with the right local name. Verified on both hosts. ROUTING IS A SEPARATE THING, and the distinction matters: passing the mutation guard does NOT make peer_send_by_name deliver to that role. Spawning deliberately does NOT claim the durable role binding (operator ruling, 2026-08-14) — claiming a role adds a name and never releases the incumbent's, so an automatic claim at spawn would EVICT whoever currently holds it: a destructive act triggered by a routine one. The spawned worker claims its role explicitly once it is up, and only then does role-addressed routing reach it. role_name is recorded on the ledger row as the spawn's stated INTENT, never as a claim. REFUSAL (operator ruling, 2026-08-14): a second spawn under a local_name that a non-terminal managed_session row already holds is refused loudly with local_name_already_held, naming the incumbent's agent_instance_id, lifecycle_state, host, host_ref and lane, plus the terminate_session call that would free the name. Never a silent uniquifying suffix — the guard's compare is exact, so 'Git-Controller-2' is simply a session that cannot mutate git — and never a silent eviction. The ordering is terminate the holder, THEN spawn the replacement. HOW THIS RELATES TO THE OTHER TWO ROLE GATES, since an adopter will meet these three in some order and reading only one of them teaches the wrong general rule: (1) THIS verb refuses a second spawn under a live local name; (2) peer_claim_role independently refuses a claim against a LIVE different-session holder with role_held_live, unless an explicit takeover is passed after operator confirmation — that gate already shipped and is NOT new here, so do not build a second one on top of it; (3) a holder that reads DEAD by the liveness window is claimable cheaply, with no explicit terminate, and this is deliberate rather than an oversight: a session that crashed can no longer release its own role, so a gate that also refused dead holders would strand that role permanently behind a session that no longer exists — a worse failure than the collision the refusal exists to prevent. Crash succession stays cheap on purpose. W4A (#8 §43.1, 2026-08-14): degraded_hooks_acknowledged (default false) is the explicit opt-in to spawn onto a host whose preflight can PROVE the worker's hooks will not run — a managed Claude Code policy listing 'hooks' in strictPluginOnlyCustomization strips hooks from every non-plugin source, including the --settings blob both drivers inject worker hooks through. Without the flag such a spawn is refused by host_cannot_spawn, naming the policy file and the offending key. With it, the spawn proceeds, the choice is recorded on the ledger row and logged loudly, and 'running degraded' stays a stated operator decision rather than something discovered later from the silence. At a same-local-name collision, synchronously probe each incumbent exact native host/ref. Only observed dead may transition through the existing legal lifecycle edge with observed_dead rationale, without terminating the host, releasing registration or evicting a role. CAS predicates include the observed host, host_ref, lifecycle_state, last_transition_at and last_heartbeat_at, including nulls. A lost CAS discards the observation, rereads the full same-name set and probes again; new incumbents require fresh evaluation. Alive and unknown/error observations retain local_name_already_held at the duplicate-process integrity boundary, with explicit observation detail. Unobservable operator hosts are unknown. Successful repair is followed by a full requery before replacement; no telemetry-age prerequisite is added.
embedding_description: Submit a bounded session-launch job and retrieve its final result by exact job id. Spawn a fleet-managed session with selector-issued capability proof; optionally durably queue exact first_go bytes to the new instance before either first-turn release, returning an immutable message/hash/recipient receipt and retaining the host on enqueue failure.
dispatch_policy_guidance: dispatch_kind is required provenance: diagnose, design, review, fix, or infrastructure. difficulty_score and selection_receipt are required; selection_receipt_required and selection_receipt_mismatch refuse before a ledger write. Capability floors and quota state are enforced by the replayed selector, never a dispatch-kind pair allowlist.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Accepted submission only: data.job_id and data.status=queued. After terminal retrieval, job.result.data carries the original operation fields; job.result.error preserves its error. Continue dependent actions only after this retrieval.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: Report acceptance with job_id. Retrieve the terminal job before reporting an instance, dispatch state, first-turn outcome, or qualification verdict. Keep uptake_pending and uptake_uncertain distinct from worker ACK.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Validation runs BEFORE the ledger write (unknown_role_class, unknown_work_class, budget_line_required, role_not_legislated, role_class_conflict, reserved_role_name, local_name_already_held) so a refused spawn never touches state. Host resolution errors (host_not_declared, host_mechanism_missing) also precede the write. host_cannot_spawn is the one failure that happens AFTER the ledger row exists — the row is transitioned straight to 'terminated' before the error surfaces, so no spawn is ever left stuck in 'spawning' for a dispatch already known to have failed. local_name_already_held names the incumbent and the terminate_session call that frees the name; the fix is to terminate the holder and re-spawn, never to add a suffix (the mutation guard's compare is exact, so a suffixed name silently loses the capability the spawn was for). host_cannot_spawn also carries the managed-policy refusal: when the host's managed Claude Code policy lists 'hooks' in strictPluginOnlyCustomization, the worker's hooks cannot run and the spawn is refused by name rather than producing a worker that answers turns while never registering. Set degraded_hooks_acknowledged to proceed anyway; it is recorded on the row.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: unknown_role_class/unknown_work_class: the caller passed a value outside the declared taxonomy. budget_line_required: budget_line was empty. role_not_legislated: role_class='principal' named a role_name with no existing role row — principal offices are fill-never-mint, not mintable through this verb. role_class_conflict: role_name already exists under a DIFFERENT role_class than requested. reserved_role_name: role_name matches the <solet>-Main pattern and has no legislated row yet. host_not_declared: an explicit blank host override was passed. host_mechanism_missing: the resolved host (override, FLEET_SESSION_HOST env, or the 'headless' default) has no driver registered in this build at all — none of 'operator'/'headless'/'tmux' matched, most likely a typo'd host name. host_cannot_spawn: the resolved driver is registered but cannot spawn right now — the 'operator' driver never spawns (degenerate by design), or the 'headless'/'tmux' driver is registered but unconfigured (missing permission mode / .mcp.json / the claude binary, or for tmux an unsupported tmux version — the error names exactly which).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For role_not_legislated, legislate the office first via plugin::agent_messaging_plugin::legislate_role (role_class='principal'), or spawn with role_class='project' instead. For host_mechanism_missing, pass a host name that is actually registered ('operator', 'headless', or 'tmux') — there is no other name to wait for; check for a typo. For host_cannot_spawn against 'headless' or 'tmux', fix the exact configuration gap the error names (permission mode, MCP config, the claude binary, or the tmux binary/version); against 'operator', launch the session manually instead — this verb cannot do it for that driver.

native_unit_ownership.order: Verified existing Unit/revision -> platform observation of generated child agi/lane/runtime/model/effort -> successful host launch -> coordinator-authored set-owner CAS -> first turn. Identity observation is never worker read-back, ACK or completion.
native_unit_ownership.receipt: Terminal successful result includes ownership_receipt with identity event, actual owner actor, Unit/revision and attempt identity. Existing native Unit owner history is append-only. Same-attempt replay adds no owner assignment; released actors and older managed attempts cannot reclaim ownership.
native_unit_ownership.failure: Host failure leaves the prior Unit owner intact and terminates the failed ledger row. spawn_owner_transfer_failed retains spawning host and exact receipt under capability_report.native_spawn_owner, with no first turn. Repeat the exact bare spawn request to recover the same alive host. For a managed failed_start caused by owner transfer, repeat dispatch_managed_work or use explicit request_retry: both reopen ownership recovery on the same attempt and retained alive host, without changing its actor or attempt number. Ordinary host failures still require a new retry attempt. Never silently launch an anonymous replacement.
native_unit_ownership.pass_condition: A successfully spawned lane has its native ownership receipt and, when first_go is supplied, its durable message/hash/recipient receipt before the driver channel receives its first turn. Every first_go retry reuses the accepted receipt and refuses changed bytes; an unconfirmed enqueue retains the host without release.
native_unit_ownership.pass_path_test: native_spawn_owner_postgres_smoke.py asserts actual child owner at driver.send and runs child native CLI read-back/start without Main set-owner.
